results.fact: Total elevation gain/loss for the route
results.correct_value: about 4,600 ft gain and loss car to car for the single-day Mineral Creek line
results.evidence: The 6,300 ft figure belongs to a different, two-day 17-mile trip to the main peak from a camp at Upper Park Lake (north couloir/north face), not to this single-day Mineral Creek south-side line. A single-day Mineral Creek ascent of the main peak records 2,360 to 6,687 ft (about 4,330 ft net, 7.7 mi RT), and a single-day ascent of the adjacent Middle Peak (6,600 ft) from the same trailhead on the same talus approach measured 4,600 ft gained and lost. 3,500 ft is below the net difference; 4,600 ft is the measured cumulative figure consistent with both.

results.fact: Which side of the mountain the standard route actually climbs
results.correct_value: Single-day Mineral Creek line: south-side talus to the southeast shoulder, traverse onto the northeast ridge, final ~400 ft to the East summit; the Park Lakes north-face-ledge line is a separate two-day route
results.evidence: The beta/face/pitch_detail text comes from a two-day 2001 trip that camped at Upper Park Lake and crossed a north-face ledge from the Main-Middle notch (17 mi, 6,300 ft) — a different route. A single-day Mineral Creek ascent leaves the trail west of the broad waterfall gully, climbs to the southeast shoulder at 6,200 ft, traverses a quarter mile to the northeast ridge and finishes up the final 400 ft; a separate description agrees the summit is generally reached via the northeast ridge from the SE shoulder with a loose class 3-4 step onto the ridge. The row's approach, itinerary, waypoint positions (SE of the summit, whereas the Main-Middle notch lies west of the East summit) and descent all describe the Mineral Creek line, so the Park Lakes text is relabelled as a different route and the pitches/waypoints renamed to the shoulder/NE-ridge line.

patches.fact: Which side of the mountain the standard route actually climbs
patches.find: From a backcountry camp at Upper or Middle Park Lake, parties ascend talus and scree toward the Main-Middle notch. The ridge crest directly above the notch quickly degenerates into class 5 terrain, so the accepted line traverses south/east onto a broad ledge system on the north face (documented as 'generally sound rock with some loose sections' for roughly the final 200 ft) to reach the summit ridge. An alternate approach climbs a north couloir to the same notch area. Both variants are described as class 3-4 scrambling with real exposure, not a walk-up.
patches.replace: From the Mineral Creek Trail, leave the tread west of the broad waterfall gully and climb off-trail through vine maple and then long south-side talus and scree to the southeast shoulder (about 6,200 ft). From the shoulder, traverse roughly a quarter mile of steep snow or talus onto the northeast ridge, then scramble the final ~400 ft up the ridge to the East (true) summit. The step onto the ridge and the upper ridge are loose, exposed class 3 with a short class 4 move or two, so test every hold. A separate, longer line from a camp at Upper Park Lake climbs the north side to the Main-Middle notch and crosses a ledge system on the north face; it is a different route, not part of this one.
